items.title: Spider-Man at 92 Percent: The Box-Office Race Ended Before the Challenger Opened
items.content_text:
Spider-Man at 92 Percent: The Box-Office Race Ended Before the Challenger Opened

On Halloween night, with two months of the year still to run, the market for 2026 at the movies is effectively settled. Polymarket's "Highest grossing movie in 2026?" contract, open since November 12, 2025, has traded $17.8 million across 14 possible winners, and it prices Spider-Man: Brand New Day at 92 percent.

The challenger is not close. Avengers: Doomsday sits at about 9 percent, while Wicked: For Good and Wuthering Heights are both under 1 percent. That gap holds even though Doomsday is tracking toward $100 million in presales alone, outpacing Spider-Man's presales by 67 percent in the tracking cited on the market page.

The calendar is the trade. The market resolves on Box Office Mojo's domestic calendar gross for 2026, so only money a film earns by December 31 counts. Spider-Man opened on July 29 and has had months to bank its total. Doomsday opens in December and gets roughly two weeks inside the window, no matter how large its opening weekend is.

The price tells the year's story. Spider-Man traded at just 32 percent on March 12, climbed through 83 percent in late October, and now sits at 92. A Nintendo sequel that once contended fell from 46 percent to 1 percent between March 13 and July 27. Final settlement waits for the December 31 data, due by January 7, 2027.

A movie question drawing $17.8 million is the point. Culture is no longer a side board on prediction markets; on the biggest film question of the year, the crowd has already called the winner.

Sources: Polymarket, RG, GambleRss

items.content_text:
Half of Google's Midterm Answers Are Now a Market

Ask Google who will win the Senate this November, and there is an even chance a market is part of the answer. A CasinoReviews.net study of 140 Google results pages across 14 US cities found Polymarket or Kalshi on page one for half of everyday forecast searches such as "election forecast" and "midterm polls."

On 112 mobile results pages, 50% showed a betting platform on page one. The platforms appeared in all eight cities tested in states where state law bans betting on elections - Houston, Phoenix, Atlanta, Philadelphia, Detroit, Charlotte, Las Vegas and Chicago - even though 24 states ban election betting outright, while federally regulated markets still offer election contracts nationwide.

The split is sharp. Kalshi appeared on all 28 pages for "senate odds" and "midterm odds," but on only 6% of forecast pages - Kalshi owns odds searches, Polymarket owns forecasts, the study found. Searchers treat markets like polls: "Polymarket polls" and "Kalshi polls" rank among the top related searches.

Yet only about 1 in 120 midterm searches uses betting or odds language, and forecast searches without that language outnumber them nearly nine to one. Across 46 states, Google Trends interest in Polymarket and Kalshi, relative to interest in the 2026 elections, showed no consistent difference between ban states and states with no such law.

Researchers checked 10 searches in each of 14 cities on October 15 and 16, 2026, with search volumes from Ahrefs covering 10,092 US keywords containing "midterm elections." Lead researcher Nikoleta Kuncheva put it plainly: most people who search for midterm predictions are not looking to place a bet - they want to know who is going to win.

Sources: CasinoReviews.net, BusinessWire

items.content_text:
From 27% to the Lead: Israel's $82 Million Market Flipped

Before Israel voted on October 27, the market had a clear favorite. On Polymarket, Gadi Eizenkot stood at 58% to be the next prime minister and Benjamin Netanyahu at 27%. Kalshi told the same story, at 52% for Eizenkot against 28% for Netanyahu, with no other candidate close.

The votes changed the board. Netanyahu now leads the same Polymarket market at 43%, with Eizenkot at 35%, in a market that has traded $82.2 million across 19 outcomes since it opened on November 14, 2025. DeFi Rate's movers board puts Netanyahu up 15 points in seven days, from 28% to 43%.

The market is not settled, because the job goes to whoever is sworn in, and that takes 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Neither bloc had a clear path to 61 in the final polls. Official results are due November 4, and the leader chosen then gets 28 days to form a government, plus up to 14 more.

The flip also drew scrutiny. Polymarket is investigating hundreds of accounts created less than an hour before polls closed at 10 p.m. in Jerusalem, Casino.org reported on October 30. The fresh wallets jointly netted over $100,000 after exit polls favored Netanyahu, one account turned $14,000 staked 12 minutes before the close into $42,000, and analysts at Polysights put potential payouts from fresh wallets at over $700,000.

It is a clean test of what these markets price: not vote share, but coalition math after the count. The $82 million board got the favorite wrong before the vote and repriced in days. Whether it also had to police its own tape is now part of the story.

Sources: Polymarket, DeFi Rate, Casino.org, RG.org

items.content_text:
91 Percent at Fight Time: Canelo's Market Left the Bookies Behind

On fight day in Riyadh, the prediction market stopped treating Canelo Alvarez's comeback as a contest. CoinStats' Saturday evening board read, at 7:11 PM ET, priced Canelo as the favourite at 91 percent on Kalshi, with $5.2 million traded in 24 hours on that venue and $6.6 million in total volume on the market, which resolves November 1. Hours earlier, the same contract sat at 74 percent on just $296K traded. Fight day did not nudge the price. It ran it over.

The stakes explain the rush. Canelo, 36 and 63-3-2, was fighting for the first time since losing to Terence Crawford in September 2025, and he was the challenger this time: unbeaten WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli, 29-0-1 with 24 knockouts, held the belt on the Mexico vs. The World card in Riyadh.

The striking gap was between the two kinds of market. Sportsbooks kept the upset alive all week: BetMGM had Canelo at -300, the best bookmaker price was 2/5, an implied chance of about 71 percent, and Mbilli was available at 13/5. Kalshi's traders, putting up millions on the day itself, priced the same comeback at 91 percent, near certainty.

The whole card traded, not just the main event. On Kalshi's undercard board, Jaime Munguia was -900 against Nikita Zon, a 90 percent implied chance, Rafael Espinoza was the biggest favourite on the card at -1567, and David Picasso was -355 against Carl Martin.

Boxing's biggest name now trades like a stock on fight day, and the exchange, not the bookmaker, posted the boldest number in the building.

items.title: Worth More Than the Bookies Combined
items.content_text:
Worth More Than the Bookies Combined

Prediction markets now have a profit story to match the volume story. In a research report released Friday, PitchBook estimates Kalshi is on course for $1.2 billion in adjusted earnings in 2026, ahead of DraftKings' guidance for the year, on $3.7 billion in gross revenue. Kalshi has already banked $2.4 billion in fee revenue before rebates this year, with records falling regularly since football season began.

The valuations are the headline. PitchBook puts Kalshi at $42.3 billion and Polymarket at $20.6 billion, a combined $62.9 billion, while Flutter and DraftKings together are worth less than $23 billion after their share prices tumbled. The estimates sit just above the roughly $40 billion and $20 billion levels the two exchanges are reportedly raising funds at, and PitchBook says the acceleration in trading volume warrants them.

The gap between the rivals is earnings, not attention. Polymarket's projected 2026 gross revenue is $842 million, with $526.9 million net and just $34.9 million in adjusted earnings, weighed down by running two exchanges, one in the U.S. and one globally. Marketing is the biggest expense at both firms, about 33 percent of Kalshi's revenue, with all of Kalshi's costs adding up to about 60 percent of revenue.

PitchBook expects the lead to widen, then narrow. By 2028 it projects Kalshi gross revenue of $8.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $3 billion, against Polymarket gross revenue of $3.2 billion and earnings of $624.3 million. Even if a court ruling cost them a quarter of U.S. sports contracts, Kalshi would still be worth $25 billion and Polymarket $14.6 billion: hurt, not ruined.

The engine underneath is volume. Kalshi set a record $5.3 billion day on a recent Saturday, a $10 billion weekend, and $25.5 billion across the seven days to October 26, taking $118.4 million in fee revenue that week. Polymarket US set its own record the same Saturday at $811.2 million. The bookies are no longer the biggest business in the room.

Sources: InGame, PitchBook

items.content_text:
Gold Joins the 15-Minute Club: Polymarket's First Market Beyond Crypto

Polymarket's fastest markets no longer stop at crypto. Its 15-minute gold and silver up-or-down markets are now live, the platform's first contracts outside crypto prices, with Chainlink as the official oracle supplying the pricing for every window.

The format is familiar, the asset is not. Traders buy shares on whether gold or silver closes a rolling 15-minute window above or below the level printed at the open. At spot near $3,980 an ounce, even a $20 move inside a window is just half a percent — a volatility contract, not a claim on the metal itself.

The scale behind the launch is the story. Chainlink and Polymarket say the partnership has already settled more than $11 billion in trading volume across Polymarket's 5- and 15-minute crypto markets. That is about 1.24 times LINK's entire market capitalization of about $8.9 billion, with LINK near $11.59 on October 31, up about 4.9 percent in 24 hours.

The crypto machine it extends is relentless: 15-minute markets settle 96 times a day, crypto accounts for $197 million traded in 24 hours on the DeFi Rate board, and Bitcoin finished up in just 49 percent of its last 1,311 Kalshi windows — 642 of them — a near coin flip where price, not direction, decides the trade.

Gold and silver are only the first step. The stated roadmap is more commodities, with equities and foreign exchange to follow, on a Polymarket US venue that operates as a CFTC-regulated designated contract market. The 15-minute club just opened its doors to traditional assets.

Sources: KuCoin, Chainlink, DeFi Rate, CoinGecko
